content: The coadministration of ciprofloxacin with drugs that prolong the QT interval may increase the risk of torsades de pointes in predisposed patients, though this risk is lower with ciprofloxacin compared to other quinolones. Erythromycin lactobionate increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. ECG monitoring is recommended when using drugs that may prolong the QT interval. Erythromycin lactobionate also increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin, conivaptan, and conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. For oral forms of conjugated estrogens, there is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora, but it increases their levels when mediated by P-glycoprotein. Similarly, it increases the levels or effects of cortisone, crizotinib, and cyclosporine through P-glycoprotein or CYP3A4 interactions. Crizotinib also increases erythromycin lactobionate levels, necessitating dose adjustments for drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. Dabrafenib decreases erythromycin lactobionate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring close monitoring. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of dactinomycin, danicopan, dapsone, daridorexant, and darunavir through P-glycoprotein or CYP3A4 interactions. Daridorexant doses should not exceed 25 mg per night when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Dasatinib and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring. Erythromycin lactobionate also increases the levels or effects of daunorubicin, deflazacort, and dexamethasone through P-glycoprotein or CYP3A4 interactions. Erythromycin lactobionate increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing adverse reactions. It decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora but increases their levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache is recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases digoxin levels via P-glycoprotein interactions and disopyramide levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate increases docetaxel levels through P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 interactions. Dolasetron and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of donepezil, doxorubicin, and dutasteride through CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein interactions. Duvelisib increases erythromycin lactobionate levels, necessitating dose adjustments for sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Erythromycin lactobionate increases efavirenz levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix increases erythromycin lactobionate levels via P-glycoprotein but decreases them through CYP3A4 metabolism. Eliglustat increases erythromycin lactobionate levels via P-glycoprotein, requiring close monitoring. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of etoposide, exemestane, and ezogabine through CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein interactions. Ezogabine and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating ECG monitoring. Fedratinib increases erythromycin lactobionate levels, requiring dose adjustments for CYP3A4 substrates. Erythromycin lactobionate increases finasteride and finerenone levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring serum potassium is recommended during finerenone initiation or dosage adjustments. Flecainide and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring. Erythromycin lactobionate increases fludrocortisone levels via P-glycoprotein interactions. Erythromycin lactobionate and fluoxetine both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating close monitoring. Erythromycin lactobionate increases fluvastatin toxicity, potentially increasing the risk of myopathy. Fluvoxamine and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring. Foscarnet and erythromycin lactobionate also prolong the QTc interval. Fostamatinib increases erythromycin lactobionate levels via P-glycoprotein, necessitating monitoring for toxicities of P-glycoprotein substrates. Fostemsavir increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters and prolongs the QTc interval at high doses. Gadobenate and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin lactobionate increases gentamicin levels via P-glycoprotein interactions. Gepirone and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring. Goserelin increases erythromycin lactobionate levels and the risk of torsades de pointes. Erythromycin lactobionate increases guanfacine levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Guanfacine dosage should be halved when coadministered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Histrelin increases erythromycin lactobionate levels and the risk of torsades de pointes. Erythromycin lactobionate increases hydrocortisone levels via P-glycoprotein interactions. Hydroxyzine increases erythromycin lactobionate toxicity and the risk of torsades de pointes. Erythromycin lactobionate increases ibrutinib levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring dose adjustments. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases ifosfamide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing therapeutic effects. Iloperidone and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring. Erythromycin lactobionate increases imatinib levels through CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein interactions. Erythromycin lactobionate increases indacaterol levels by modulating P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 activities. Indacaterol and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Erythromycin lactobionate increases indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein interactions. Erythromycin lactobionate increases irinotecan levels through P-glycoprotein interactions. It also increases isavuconazonium sulfate and isradipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Istradefylline increases erythromycin lactobionate levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein interactions, necessitating dose reductions for sensitive substrates. Erythromycin lactobionate increases itraconazole levels through CYP3A4 metabolism or P-glycoprotein interactions. It also increases ivacaftor levels, requiring dose reductions when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ivacaftor increases erythromycin lactobionate levels via P-glycoprotein interactions. Erythromycin lactobionate increases ivermectin levels via P-glycoprotein interactions. It also increases ivosidenib levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating monitoring for QTc prolongation. Erythromycin lactobionate increases ketoconazole levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, and ketoconazole reciprocally increases erythromycin lactobionate levels. Erythromycin lactobionate increases lapatinib levels via P-glycoprotein interactions. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring. Erythromycin lactobionate increases larotrectinib levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Lenacapavir increases erythromycin lactobionate levels, necessitating monitoring for adverse reactions. Erythromycin lactobionate and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval, requiring ECG monitoring. Letermovir increases erythromycin lactobionate levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Leuprolide increases erythromycin lactobionate toxicity and the risk of torsades de pointes. Erythromycin lactobionate increases levamlodipine levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring dose adjustments. Both erythromycin lactobionate and levofloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Levoketoconazole increases erythromycin lactobionate levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. It increases loperamide levels via P-glycoprotein interactions. Lorlatinib decreases erythromycin lactobionate levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate increases lumateperone levels through CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring dose reductions. It also increases lurasidone levels through CYP3A4 metabolism.
